policy_title: Invest £36 Billion in Local Transport Infrastructure
stated: The Conservative Party will invest £36 billion saved from cancelling the second phase of HS2 into local roads, rail, and buses to drive regional growth, including £8.3 billion to fill potholes and resurface roads, and additional funding for smaller cities, towns, and city regions.

source.quote: Invest £36 billion in local roads, rail and buses to drive regional growth, including £8.3 billion to fill potholes and resurface roads, funded by cancelling the second phase of HS2.

bearing_set.reason: Improved local rail, bus, and road connectivity in smaller cities and towns directly affects residents' ability to access employment, potentially raising effective wages and reducing in-work poverty in underserved regions.

The policy simultaneously funds road expansion (which tends to induce car traffic and raise emissions) and buses/rail (which can shift modal share and cut emissions); at £36bn scale the net environmental effect is non-negligible and genuinely contested.

Pothole repair reduces vehicle damage and maintenance costs borne by households; bus and rail investment can lower household transport expenditure, both concrete mechanisms affecting disposable income.
£36bn of local road, rail and bus investment directly targets regional productivity, business connectivity and economic opportunity — the core indicators of prosperity and living standards.

The policy explicitly redirects spending from HS2 Phase 2 (which was designed to boost Northern city connectivity) to local/regional networks; whether this narrows or widens the north-south gap is genuinely contested and non-negligible in scale.

The £36bn is claimed as savings from HS2 cancellation, but the size and availability of those savings is independently disputed; if overstated, the plan adds to borrowing or crowds out other commitments, materially affecting the debt path.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear clearly: O13 (core purpose — regional economic opportunity), O14 (redistribution of connectivity investment between regions), O6 (contested environmental net effect of road vs public-transport spend), and O12 (fiscal credibility of the HS2-savings funding claim). Effects on O2, O4, O15 would be incidental rather than material at this stage of analysis.
